asked: When is an Investigational Device Exemption required and what are the significant risk criteria?
answer: An Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) is required for clinical investigations of medical devices that meet the criteria outlined in 21 CFR 812.28(a)(2). The significant risk criteria require supporting information as described in 21 CFR 812.28(a)(2)(i) to be submitted, while non-significant risk investigations require supporting information as described in 21 CFR 812.28(a)(2)(ii) to be submitted. The available regulatory sources do not provide enough information to answer this. [3][4]

asked: What sanitation requirements apply to plant and grounds under Part 117 Subpart B?
answer:
1. Grounds. The grounds about a food plant under the control of the operator must be kept in a condition that will protect against the contamination of food. The methods for adequate maintenance of grounds must include: [1]  
2. Properly storing equipment, removing litter and waste, and cutting weeds or grass within the immediate vicinity of the plant that may constitute an attractant, breeding place, or harborage for pests. [2]  
3. Maintaining roads, yards, and parking lots so that they do not constitute a source of contamination in areas where food is exposed. [3]  
4. Buildings, fixtures, and other physical facilities of the plant must be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition and must be kept in repair adequate to prevent food from becoming adulterated. Cleaning and sanitizing of utensils and equipment must be conducted in a manner that protects against allergen cross-contact and contamination of food, food-contact surfaces, or food-packaging materials. [4]  
5. Cleaning compounds and sanitizing agents used in cleaning and sanitizing procedures must be free from undesirable microorganisms and must be safe and adequate under the conditions of use. Compliance with this requirement must be verified by any effective means, including purchase of these substances under a letter of guarantee or certification or examination of these substances for contamination. Only the following toxic materials may be used or stored in a plant where food is processed or exposed: [6]  
6. The water supply must be adequate for the operations intended and must be derived from an adequate source. Any water that contacts food, food-contact surfaces, or food-packaging materials must be safe and of adequate sanitary quality. Running water at a suitable temperature, and under pressure as needed, must be provided in all areas where required for the processing of food, for the cleaning of equipment, utensils, and food-packaging materials, or for employee sanitary facilities. [8]

asked: Which products are subject to FDA tobacco authority under the deeming rule, and what does Part 1100 address?
answer:
21 CFR part 1100  
Subject: tobacco products, FDA tobacco authority, deeming rule  
Tobacco products: Cigarettes, cigarette tobacco, roll-your-own tobacco, smokeless tobacco, and any tobacco product containing nicotine not made or derived from tobacco are subject to the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.  
Deeming rule: FDA deems all other products meeting the definition of tobacco product under section 201(rr) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, except accessories of such other tobacco products, to be subject to the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. [1][2]

Tobacco authority: FDA deems all other tobacco products, except accessories of such other tobacco products, subject to chapter IX of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and its implementing regulations. [2]

Deeming rule: If a product made or derived from tobacco that is intended for human consumption is intended for use for any of the purposes described in paragraph (a) or (b) of this section, the product is not a tobacco product as defined in section 201(rr) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and will be subject to regulation as a drug, device, or combination product. [3]

Deeming rule: (a) The product is intended for use in the diagnosis of disease or other conditions, or in the cure, mitigation, treatment or prevention of disease, including use in the cure or treatment of nicotine addiction (e.g., smoking cessation), relapse prevention, or relief of nicotine withdrawal symptoms; [4]

Deeming rule: (b) The product is intended to affect the structure or any function of the body in any way that is different from effects related to nicotine that were commonly and legally claimed in the marketing of cigarettes and smokeless tobacco products prior to March 21, 2000. [5]

21 CFR 211.192 requires a written record of the investigation and include the conclusions and followup [7]. 
21 CFR 211.194(a) requires laboratory records to include complete data derived from all tests necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards [11]. 
21 CFR 211.196 requires distribution records to include the name and strength of the product and description of the dosage form, name and address of the consignee, date and quantity shipped, and lot or control number of the drug product [12].
